judged_by: Matched by a Claude Opus 5.5 agent on 2026-11-25; not yet checked by the labeler.

central_claim.note: Both halves, hesitancy and booster uptake.

evidence.note: Zip codes matched to 2020 election vote shares (E3). Online survey of 683 participants, March 8 to April 19, 2023, without Qualtrics Panels or the convenience sample (E1 partial). N only, no screening figures (E2 partial). Self-reported status and 'validated hesitancy scales', the AAVS items only in the quote (E5 partial). 'Validated' is close to the paper's CFA and reliability check, not flagged.
Linear and logistic regressions with the interaction and full controls.

key_findings.note: Hesitancy half of F1; the status half is not stated.

Both hesitancy interactions significant, steeper in conservative climates; liberals-regardless part not stated in the slot. 'Effect of conservatism' not flagged (the paper speaks of moderation and average effects).
Vaccine-status interaction not significant with the mandates explanation (F4). Booster-status interaction significant, without shape (F3 partial).
Conservative half of F3 (60% vs under 35%); liberal half missing, so F3 is not joined.

scope_and_limits.note: Effect modification not tested, with the consequence (average effects, may mask subgroup heterogeneity).
'Influences' wording not flagged, following the earlier match of the same phrasing.

theoretical_positioning.note: Both literatures separately, interaction 'for the first time' (paper: 'first assessment', p.7).

interlocutor_claim.note: Fridman, Levin and Heiman are refs 6, 7 and 8 in the cited range 6-12: correct.
Rönn et al. (ref. 19) correct; vaccination-rate half of I3 (the booster-rate study, ref. 20, is not given). 'Climate effect' not flagged, as in earlier matches.
